entry.idea: ElevenLabs makes software that turns text into realistic human speech and lets businesses build voice agents that can talk to customers.
entry.lesson: Once a core AI skill crosses a quality bar, wrap it in easy products for both solo creators and big enterprises, and the market splits into many paying use cases.
entry.name: ElevenLabs

growth.reason: Its valuation jumped from about $3bn to about $11bn in roughly a year, backed by a much bigger funding round.

market.reason: AI voice and speech tools can be used by almost any company that makes content, runs customer service, or builds software, worldwide.

tech.reason: Its expressive, multilingual speech generation is good enough to be used by Disney and Epic Games, which would take a strong team a year or two to match.

entry.twist: Its voices sound natural and expressive in more than 70 languages, so film studios and game makers use it for characters and dubbing, not just robotic text-to-speech.
entry.who_pays: Large companies such as Stripe, Cisco, Deutsche Telekom and Salesforce pay for API access and voice agents; creators pay to make audiobooks, ads and podcasts.
entry.why_now: AI voice has become good enough that big, well-known brands are now willing to put it into real products instead of just experimenting with it.
